evidence.supportingExcerpt: Affinity describes one binding interaction under stated conditions. For a simple one-to-one equilibrium a lower dissociation constant (KD, a concentration often given in nanomolar units) means tighter binding, whereas papers that report association constants (per molar) read the other way, with a higher value meaning tighter binding, so compare like with like. Avidity is the combined strength of several contacts and depends on target density, spacing and the number of binding sites. In one set of experiments the Fab fragment of an anti-HLA-A2 antibody had an affinity of 1.9 x 10^7 per molar while the bivalent F(ab)2 or IgG showed an avidity of 1.3 x 10^9 per molar on cells (Ways and Parham, 1983). A cell-binding result for a multivalent product is therefore not its single-site affinity; ask which assay was used and how many sites took part.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Developability asks whether a molecule can be produced, purified, formulated and stored, stays soluble and stable, does not aggregate and does not bind unrelated molecules. Jain et al. (2017) expressed 137 clinical-stage antibody sequences as IgG1 and measured a dozen biophysical properties to describe the range seen in clinical-stage antibodies. Kinna et al. The VHH preparations had a higher reported thermal-unfolding midpoint and lower predicted aggregation and positive-surface-patch scores. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Measurement rows and their limits. evidence.supportingExcerpt: A primary comparison of bispecific constructs found different lytic activity despite similar antigen-binding affinity, with epitope geometry contributing to the result. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Four routes to candidate binders are described in primary experiments. In 1976 Köhler and Milstein fused spleen cells from immunised mice with myeloma cells; the hybrid lines grew in culture and about 10 per cent of them showed activity against the sheep red cells used to immunise, so each line had to be tested for what it made. In 1990 McCafferty and colleagues displayed complete antibody variable domains on filamentous phage, showed that the phage bound antigen specifically, and isolated rare phage (one in a million) by affinity chromatography. In 1997 Boder and Wittrup displayed single-chain antibody fragments on yeast and used flow cytometry to compare binding kinetics, selecting a variant with a threefold lower dissociation rate. In 2023 Watson and colleagues designed binders to five targets with the RFdiffusion network, took 95 designs per target, expressed and purified them from E. coli and screened them by single-point biolayer interferometry at 10 micromolar; binding at or above half the maximal response of a positive control counted as success, the overall rate was 19 per cent, and full titrations on a subset of designs showed nanomolar affinities. Each result is a measured interaction under stated laboratory conditions. A selected, enriched or designed sequence is a candidate; the studies do not test activity in cells in a patient, absence of binding to healthy tissue, or clinical benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: There is no transferable best affinity. A measured affinity describes an interaction in a specified model, while behaviour also depends on target density, geometry, exposure and unwanted recognition. Bluemel et al. (2010) found BiTE constructs with similar affinity but very different lysis. Kinna et al. (2026) chose ten VHH and scFv pairs with comparable domain targeting and KD of 10^-9 to 10^-11 molar and still found differences in stability, in vitro cytokine release and survival in an acute myeloid leukaemia xenograft; the tumour was the human AML-derived MOLM-14 cell line in NSG mice, with generally five mice per group. The authors identify use of a single donor from the preceding in-vitro experiments as a limitation. This does not establish general superiority of either format or compare clinical products in patients.

Format changes what is tested. A soluble molecule must stay intact and usable through manufacture, storage and exposure, and adding binding units or a chemical cargo can change its behaviour (Junutula et al., 2008, anti-MUC16 conjugate in mice, rats and monkeys). A CAR fixes the binder to a membrane and links contact to signalling, so spacer reach, target position, expression and clustering matter (Hudecek et al., 2015; Long et al., 2015). The same recognition sequence therefore does not guarantee the same performance.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Sequence difficulty. Chain association (aggregation) of growing peptides blocks coupling, and double coupling does not help because the cause is intermolecular association; introducing removable backbone protection improved handling, quality and yield of several challenging sequences (Abdel-Aal et al., 2014). Washing removes soluble material but does not repair a faulty chain. This study did not make every peptide equally easy.

In solid-phase peptide synthesis the growing chain is held on a resin while protected amino acids are added one at a time and soluble reagents are washed away; the finished chain is then cleaved from the resin. Sequence changes how hard this is: peptides rich in aggregation-prone sequences are difficult, and a 2014 report described automated backbone protection that improved handling, quality and yield of several challenging sequences. For personalised cancer vaccines, an automated flow synthesiser made 30-mer peptides in under 35 minutes and 15 to 16-mers in under 20 minutes, with purity comparable to or higher than other methods (Truex et al., 2020). The same paper reports what the earlier route cost: of 598 immunising peptides designed and ordered in earlier studies, 400 (67 per cent) could be synthesised and purified to at least 95 per cent purity, with an average lead time of 18 to 20 weeks for 20 peptides, and a commercial vendor returned 10 of 29 test peptides at more than 95 per cent HPLC purity; these 29 peptides had been deliberately selected because they were particularly difficult and time-consuming to make, rather than as a typical vendor workload. In that paper mass spectrometry of the unpurified peptides showed the desired mass as the main product for all 29, and purity was measured separately by analytical reverse-phase HPLC. Synthesis, purification, identity testing and lot release are separate steps, and a peptide that is made and pure has not been shown to prime T cells or to benefit a patient.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The single question to ask: is this feature deliberately reused across recipients, or selected for this recipient? Personalisation may concern an antigen sequence, a receptor sequence, the person's own cells or a combination, and need not mean that every reagent or step is redesigned. The answer depends on the program.

Individualised products reuse some components and personalise others, and the two need separate evidence. In the phase 1 study of autogene cevumeran in resected pancreatic cancer (Rojas et al., 2023), individual vaccines of up to 20 neoantigens per patient were made in real time as uridine mRNA-lipoplex nanoparticles; 16 patients received atezolizumab and the vaccine, 15 subsequently received mFOLFIRINOX chemotherapy, and new neoantigen-specific T cells were detected in 8 of the 16 patients, and it shows one defined design carrying individual messages, not that all RNA vaccines share a recipe or outcome. In mice, a peptide-TLR-7/8a conjugate platform was built to self-assemble into nanoparticles of uniform size (about 20 nm) whatever the peptide, to address the physicochemical variability of neoantigens (Lynn et al., 2020). For autologous CAR T cells, FDA's 2024 guidance notes variability in the starting cells and recommends maintaining chain of identity from collection to administration, with at least two unique identifiers on labels of autologous products. A shared process and specification can support consistent handling and repeatable testing, but they do not establish that a new sequence or a changed process is equivalent to an earlier one, that a lot made for one recipient can be accepted on another recipient's results, or that the encoded targets are presented and recognised in a patient. 'Platform' here is a descriptive term for reuse, not a regulatory designation.

In the phase 1 study of autogene cevumeran in resected pancreatic cancer (Rojas et al., 2023), individual vaccines of up to 20 neoantigens per patient were made in real time as uridine mRNA-lipoplex nanoparticles; 16 patients received atezolizumab and the vaccine, 15 subsequently received mFOLFIRINOX chemotherapy, and new neoantigen-specific T cells were detected in 8 of the 16 patients, and it shows one defined design carrying individual messages, not that all RNA vaccines share a recipe or outcome. In mice, a peptide-TLR-7/8a conjugate platform was built to self-assemble into nanoparticles of uniform size (about 20 nm) whatever the peptide, to address the physicochemical variability of neoantigens (Lynn et al., 2020). For autologous CAR T cells, FDA's 2024 guidance notes variability in the starting cells and recommends maintaining chain of identity from collection to administration, with at least two unique identifiers on labels of autologous products. A shared process and specification can support consistent handling and repeatable testing, but they do not establish that a new sequence or a changed process is equivalent to an earlier one, that a lot made for one recipient can be accepted on another recipient's results, or that the encoded targets are presented and recognised in a patient. 'Platform' here is a descriptive term for reuse, not a regulatory designation.

FDA's November 2026 guidance aims for every released lot to have the ability to achieve the intended therapeutic effect and expects the relationship between a measured attribute and the product's mechanism of action to be supported by characterisation, nonclinical or clinical studies; where the mechanism is not fully understood, a statistical relationship such as a correlation with outcomes may help. FDA's November 2026 final potency-assurance guidance supersedes its January 2011 potency-tests guidance. Its scope is cellular and gene therapy biological products regulated under section 351 of the U.S. Public Health Service Act. Potency assurance includes process and material controls, in-process evidence, release assays, stability and in-use handling; a release assay alone does not establish the clinical benefit of a particular lot. Federal Register notice 2026-22427, published 3 November 2026, announces the final guidance and finalises the December 2023 draft.
